title: Ethiopian Coffee Truffles
author: Chef Haile
desc: Ethiopian Coffee Truffles — Kilimanjaro-quality Ethiopian arabica espresso blended with dark chocolate, cardamom, and honey, set and rolled in sesame seeds or crushed pistachios. The modern Ethiopian café's most sophisticated sweet — celebrating the birthplace of coffee.
longDesc: Ethiopian coffee truffles are the contemporary Ethiopian café's most proud dessert offering — combining the country's two greatest food traditions (coffee and honey) with dark chocolate and cardamom into a truffle of extraordinary complexity.
ingredients: // Rolling: toasted sesame seeds or cocoa powder
steps: Heat cream until just simmering. Remove from heat.
Add chopped chocolate. Wait 2 minutes. Stir until smooth.
Add espresso, honey, and cardamom. Stir well.
Cool at room temperature 30 minutes, then refrigerate 2 hours.
Scoop with a teaspoon. Roll into balls between cold palms.
Roll in sesame seeds or cocoa powder.
chefTips: Ethiopian arabica espresso is significantly more complex than any other origin — the floral notes make these truffles distinctly Ethiopian.
Cold hands are essential for rolling — warm palms melt the ganache.
The sesame coating is Ethiopian; the cocoa coating is more French — both are excellent.
commonMistakes: Warm hands when rolling — ganache melts.
cookingScience: The ganache is an emulsion of fat (chocolate butter fat) and water (cream and espresso). The honey's invert sugars prevent crystallisation and keep the ganache smooth. At refrigeration temperature, the cocoa butter in the chocolate partially crystallises, providing the firm-but-yielding truffle texture.
sustainabilityTips: Ethiopian arabica coffee — the birthplace of coffee, most sustainable when sourced directly from Ethiopian farmers.
culturalNote: Ethiopian coffee truffles are the modern Ethiopian café's proudest offering — combining the country's greatest gift to the world (arabica coffee) with the dessert format of global fine dining. To eat an Ethiopian coffee truffle is to taste the birthplace of coffee in its most refined form.
